The size-specialized allocation entry points are reached only through mallocScanTable and mallocNoScanTable, which runtime.mallocgc indexes only when sizeSpecializedMallocEnabled is true. That constant requires goexperiment.SizeSpecializedMalloc, and goc selects internal/goexperiment's files with go/build's default tool tags, which do not include goexperiment.sizespecializedmalloc for the Go 1.26.1 toolchain this repository builds against, so exp_sizespecializedmalloc_off.go is selected. All 66 functions in the file are therefore compiled but unreachable. The live families are runtime.mallocgcTiny, mallocgcSmallNoscan, mallocgcSmallScanNoHeader, mallocgcSmallScanHeader and mallocgcLarge in runtime/malloc.go, which the alloc/* capabilities cover. TestSizeSpecializedMallocIsDisabledForThisBuild proves the configuration boundary. See RUNTIME_PLAN.md section 6.1.
Runtime pinning backs supported public APIs and needs direct semantic coverage.
Runtime diagnostic logging is required on unusual failure and debugging paths.
Heap dump support is an explicit diagnostic path that needs a subprocess test.
Profiling buffer behavior requires explicit profiling and overflow tests.
